notes: Goods vehicles, buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles over 3500 kg GVM, whatever the body. Comes before the light commercial rules, so a goods-registered ute or cab-chassis over 3500 kg is heavy. class_map.csv holds NZTA's own 3.5 tonne line: for goods vehicles (NA up to it, NB over it) and for omnibuses (MD1 and MD2 up to it, MD3 and over).

vehicle_types: PASSENGER CAR/VAN|GOODS VAN/TRUCK/UTILITY|BUS|MOTOR CARAVAN|SPECIAL PURPOSE VEHICLE
notes: Utes, by body, whatever type NZTA registers them under: a ute registered as a passenger vehicle is light commercial. No weight bound, so a passenger-registered ute over 3500 kg, and a ute with no recorded GVM, are light commercial by the body alone.
A goods vehicle's cab-chassis or flat-deck body. No weight bound here; the ones over 3500 kg were taken by rule 1.
Goods vans up to and including 3500 kg GVM. A van with no recorded GVM matches nothing here (rule 15). Vans registered as passenger vehicles are people movers and take rule 6
Minibuses and light buses up to and including 3500 kg GVM, whatever the body. class_map.csv MD1 and MD2 are NZTA's omnibuses up to 3.5 tonnes.

Passenger vehicles whose canonical make and model model_segment.csv marks suv, at any confidence, with the vehicle year bounds that file states. A passenger-registered ute is light commercial (rule 2) before it can be an SUV. Passenger-registered vehicles over 3500 kg are not in rule 1's list and stay here.

Passenger cars and vans, people movers and sports cars included, whose canonical make and model model_segment.csv marks car, at any confidence, with the vehicle year bounds that file states. Passenger means only these models.

Every other passenger-registered vehicle of these bodies: a model model_segment.csv marks unresolved, a model it has no row for, and a model whose vehicle year is outside the year bounds of its row. Not known to be a car or an SUV, so not counted as either; the file's coverage is what shrinks this value.

Motor caravans up to and including 3500 kg GVM: the industry files them under their base vehicle, and NZTA's class agrees (class_map.csv lists MOTOR CARAVAN under NA, goods vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes). Their class is not tested. A motor caravan with no recorded GVM matches nothing here (rule 12).

Special purpose vehicles up to and including 3500 kg GVM that NZTA classes NA. class_map.csv: NA is a goods vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes, the one class of NZTA's table that is goods and up to that line; NB, NC and an omnibus class are not up to it, OTH is a code only and has no meaning in the table. A special purpose vehicle over 3500 kg is heavy (rule 1) whatever its class.
Special purpose vehicles up to and including 3500 kg GVM whose NZTA class rule 10 does not name: any other class, or no class recorded.
Motor caravans and special purpose vehicles with no recorded GVM (NZTA writes 0): neither the over 3500 kg line nor the up to 3500 kg line can be applied, whatever the class.
A goods vehicle of a body the light commercial rules do not name (trucks, articulated trucks, goods-rated station wagons) at 3500 kg or less. Over 3500 kg they are heavy (rule 1).
Three-wheelers (motor tricycles) that NZTA registers as passenger vehicles: not a car or van by body.
A goods vehicle or bus with no recorded GVM that no body rule above took (vans, minibuses, trucks): its mass is unknown, so neither the light nor the heavy line can be applied.
